intent: Browser, Go projections, and the sidecar retain the same NIP-01 replaceable winner regardless of delivery order.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Newer signed created_at wins; at equal timestamps the lowest event ID wins, including tombstones and replay.
Domain time cannot revive a losing wire event. Legacy logical-coordinate merges consider only each coordinate's retained winner.
Latest archive reads and fleet/runtime/FIPS selectors use lowest-ID ties.
Successive LLM workflow revisions use successive publication timestamps, not lexical ID growth; replay does not invent an older revision.

related_issue.reason: Accepted and applied are separate facts on one addressable status coordinate. Either phase can have the lowest signed ID; NIP-01 does not assign terminal-phase precedence.
related_issue.evidence: TestConfigStatusNIP01DoesNotImplyAppliedPrecedence uses the production signer, publisher, policy and SQLite store in both arrival orders, with both possible phase winners.
